exposure: community-based educational interventions (e.g., home visits, group workshops, mobile health applications, digital platforms)
outcome: maternal and child nutrition knowledge, attitudes, and practices
cohort: Children and mothers in low- and middle-income countries participating in community-based educational interventions aimed at stunting prevention, as observed in various experimental studies (RCTs and quasi-experimental research).
finding: Community-based educational interventions effectively reduce stunting and improve nutrition-related behaviors such as dietary diversity, exclusive breastfeeding, and complementary feeding practices in low- and middle-income countries, with culturally adapted and sustained programs demonstrating the most effectiveness.
country: Indonesia, Kenya, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, China, Peru
